passages.quote:
This notice sets out how the Public Sector Fraud Authority Enforcement Unit (the “Enforcement Unit”, which is part of the Cabinet Office), will use your personal data, and your rights in relation to that data.

The Data Protection Act 2018 (the DPA, which is UK’s implementation of the General Data Protection Regulation) sets out eight principles for the fair and lawful obtaining, recording, use and security of personal information. The act works in two ways:

it gives you, as an individual, certain rights

it ensures that we, as an organisation, are open about how the information is stored and used.

Purpose of processing your personal data

We collect and use personal data so that we can carry out our legal and official functions to assist the government in the prevention, identification, detection and prosecution of criminal offences including non-fraudulent offences and for the recovery of the proceeds of fraud including inappropriately obtained bounce back loans. There is no other reasonable and less intrusive way to achieve this purpose. Personal data has the same meaning as that set out by the Information Commissioner’s Office guidance on Data Protection - it is any information relating to an identified or identifiable living individual.

The actions the Enforcement Unit may take will vary between cases and will depend upon the legal powers available to the Enforcement Unit. Actions could include investigation, recovery, sanctions, penalties and prosecution, and working with other departments, public sector bodies and law enforcement to undertake these and related actions.

All personal data we hold will ultimately be for law enforcement purposes or for the exercise of a function of government department, regardless of whether or not cases are disposed of in a civil or criminal manner.

Types of personal data processed

Personal data items include but are not limited to:

Full name

Postal address

Telephone number

Date of Birth

IP Address

Email address

Bank Account information

Credit risk data

Asset data

Contract information

Identification documents (e.g. Passport and driving licence)

Data hosted on publicly accessible social media

Company directorships

Director disqualifications

Previous prosecutions

National Insurance Number

Known associates

Criminal records data

Data on third parties (family, known associates): The Enforcement Unit will seek any evidence of complicity in the offence, or in the dispersal of assets from the offence, both of which are criminal offences.

We will also process any other personal data relevant to the investigation of an offence or enforcement action taken against suspected fraud , other allegations of criminality or to enable the recovery of funds.

We also engage in activity to pursue repayment of public funds where we believe these have been paid to someone who is not entitled to them. These interventions may lead to voluntary repayment which can avoid formal action.

Sensitive personal data may be required in order to produce successful investigative outcomes and enforcement action including recovery of funds . Sensitive data will only be processed when it is relevant to a fraud or recovery investigation and there is a lawful basis to do so.

Lawful basis for processing

We process personal data submitted to us in two ways, depending on the context:

Law Enforcement Purposes: Material may be referred to us in accordance with Part 3 of the Data Protection Act 2018. In these cases, the processing is necessary for the performance of a task carried out for law enforcement purposes by a competent authority. The Cabinet Office is a Competent Authority as defined in Section 1 of Schedule 7 of the DPA 2018, and the PSFA Enforcement Unit exercises these functions as part of the Cabinet Office. The PSFA does not carry out sensitive processing for law enforcement purposes.

Exercise of a Crown Function: Once we receive the data, it may also become necessary for the Enforcement Unit to process it in the exercise of its functions under paragraph 8(d) of Part 2 of the Data Protection Act 2018. This paragraph allows processing for “the exercise of a function of the Crown, a Minister of the Crown or a government department.” While the referring department may not be directly exercising this function, the PSFA’s use of the data falls under this category.

Under Article 9(2)(g) UK GDPR, our legal basis for processing special category data is:

processing is necessary for reasons of substantial public interest

Under section 10(3) of the Data Protection Act 2018, the Schedule 1 condition relied upon by the Enforcement Unit is paragraph 6:

the processing is necessary for the exercise of a function of the Crown, a Minister of the Crown or a government department; and

is necessary for reasons of substantial public interest.

Our sources of personal data

Personal data is obtained by us from a variety of sources, including government departments and public sector bodies as well as other sources including commercial entities, and publicly available information.

The Enforcement Unit may observe, monitor, record and retain data on the internet which is available to anyone. This is known as ‘Open Source’ material and includes news report internet sites, commercial databases, Companies House and Land Registry records, blogs and social networking sites where no privacy settings have been applied.
